title: Dead Drop vectors vs spec: rate-limit and POST success response codes conflict
description:
test/vectors/deaddrop.json pins two response codes that contradict spec/12-apps.md 18.9 and the completed Python oracle (lichen/coap/resources/deaddrop.py, green pytest):

1. rate_limit_rejection vector: expected.response_code=163 (5.03 Service Unavailable). Spec 18.9 'Exceeding limits returns: 4.29 Too Many Requests with Retry-After for rate limits'. Python oracle returns aiocoap.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS (157) for rate limiting and reserves 163 for storage_full. Vector description itself says 'rate limit (5.03)'.

2. All post_submission/oscore_wrapped success vectors: expected.response_code=69 (2.05 Content). Spec 18.9 and LCI 17.5.8 say POST returns '2.01 Created' (65) with Location-Path; Python oracle returns CREATED (65).

Rust implementation (lichen-client::deaddrop, bead project-LICHEN-worker6-l1qw.9.14.8.2) follows spec+Python (4.29 for rate limit, 2.01 for POST success); vector tests document both divergences instead of matching the defective pins. Also noted: senml_payload hex in canonical_senml_payload, ttl_clamped_to_max, oscore_group_context, oscore_e2e_post_pickup_roundtrip is malformed CBOR (short length headers); senml_payload_decoded is the normative form the Python oracle uses. Decide whether to fix the vectors or change the spec.
